notes: The four problem sets of the IAP course (Lagrangian mechanics, central forces, small oscillations, Hamiltonian mechanics). Units are the problem sets and exams whose question types are recorded in research/questions/college/physics.jsonl; examples are those question kinds. robots.txt: Allow /.

units.title: Problem Set 1
examples: pendulum equation of motion from the Euler–Lagrange equation; small-angle solution
derive N Euler–Lagrange equations from the principle of least action
free-particle Lagrangian under a Galilean transformation
projectile from L = ½mv² − mgz: equations of motion and landing time

units.title: Problem Set 2
examples: energy conservation from the Lagrangian; when E ≠ T + U
two-body Lagrangian: total momentum conserved via CM coordinates
pendulum hanging from a sliding sled: Lagrangian, EOM, response to an impulse
flyball governor rotating at constant Ω: Lagrangian and equations of motion
least-time path (brachistochrone) by the calculus of variations

units.title: Problem Set 3
examples: virial theorem for a harmonic oscillator by direct averaging
cross-section for back-scattering off a hard sphere
small oscillations of the flyball governor about equilibrium
damped and driven oscillator: regimes and steady-state amplitude and phase

units.title: Problem Set 4
examples: Hamiltonian and Hamilton's equations of a harmonic oscillator; phase-space trajectories
Hamiltonian of the Kepler problem in spherical coordinates; conserved momenta, reduction to r
check a canonical transformation and find its generating function
mass on a string winding around a fixed spool: Lagrangian and conserved quantities
